chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rifa'ah, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and one of them asked him about the ornaments, whether there is Zakat upon it. He said: No, even if it reached one hundred thousand.

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: Is Zakat due on gold and silver ornaments in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that personal ornaments (*al-huliy*) are exempt from Zakat, distinguishing them from trade goods or stored wealth. The specific mention of 'one hundred thousand' underscores that the exemption is intrinsic to the item's nature as adornment rather than dependent on its monetary value reaching the *nisab* threshold. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential view that items intended for personal use and beauty are not subject to the obligatory alms tax.
